hero.subheadline: A 90 second practice drill for digital arrest scam calls. A fictional officer calls, you answer in chat, then a kind debrief shows the one habit to keep.

notice.text: This is a practice drill. The officer and the agency are fictional, and nothing here is a real call.

lines: A scam call is built to rush you
Rehearsal is how you slow it down

benefits.title: What one drill leaves you with
benefits.lead: Four things you meet in the order the drill gives them.

items.title: Hear the pressure in a safe place
items.body: The officer pushes for secrecy and urgency on purpose. You feel the shape of the call without any of the risk.

items.title: See the moment you complied
items.body: The debrief marks the first request you followed, with the words you actually used.

items.title: Leave with one habit
items.body: Every drill closes on a single habit, such as hanging up and calling the number on your card.

items.title: Bring a family member
items.body: Create a private link for one person and take the same drill together.

steps.title: Open the drill
steps.body: Choose a language and tap Try a 90 second drill. There is no account, no payment and no microphone needed.

steps.title: Answer the call in chat
steps.body: A fictional officer of a fictional agency asks for secrecy, then for money. Type what you would really say.

steps.title: Read the debrief
steps.body: The debrief shows the moments that mattered, the first request you followed, and the one habit to practise.

truth.title: What this is and is not
is: A practice drill for spotting a digital arrest scam call
A short, kind debrief written from the rules of the drill, not from a guess
Free, with no account, no payment and no microphone needed
is_not: Not protection from fraud, and not a measure of your risk
Not a test of you. There is no pass and no fail
Not official advice from any agency, bank or telecom

items.title: No real details
items.body: Never share an OTP, card number, PIN or account detail. The drill warns you when a message looks like personal data.

items.title: Stop any time
items.body: End drill stays on screen for the whole call, and chat stays available if the microphone is not.

items.title: Delete when you like
items.body: Delete the transcript and the debrief from the debrief screen. Anything left is removed after seven days.

items.question: What is a digital arrest scam?
items.answer: Someone claims to be from the police, the CBI, the ED or customs and says you are under digital arrest. No agency asks you to stay on a video call or to move money to prove your innocence.

items.question: Is any of this real?
items.answer: No. The officer, the agency and the case are fictional. The drill exists so you can hear the pressure once without any risk.

items.question: Do I need to give a phone number or an email address?
items.answer: No. There is no account. A drill needs only the link you opened, and the browser tab can be closed at any time.

items.question: What does the drill keep?
items.answer: Your messages and the debrief, so the debrief can be shown back to you. Anything left is removed after seven days, and you can delete the session from the debrief screen.

items.question: Will this stop a scammer?
items.answer: No. Practice is not protection. It may help you notice the pressure sooner and reach the habit that ends the call.

items.question: Is it free?
items.answer: Yes. There is no price, no plan and nothing to buy.

items.question: Does it work on my phone?
items.answer: Yes. The drill runs in a browser and in the Android app. If the microphone is unavailable, the chat still works.

items.question: What if I type something real, like an OTP?
items.answer: The drill flags messages that look like personal data and reminds you not to share them. In a real call, never share an OTP, a card number, a PIN or an account detail.

items.question: Can I take the drill with my family?
items.answer: Yes. Create a private link and send it to one person. The link expires on the date shown when you create it, and the debrief can be shared with a report link.

items.question: Who made this?
items.answer: Dry Run is a small practice project. It is not run by any agency, bank or telecom.

final.title: Start with one short drill
final.body: Ninety seconds, one fictional officer, and one habit to keep.

footer.notice: Dry Run is a practice drill. It is not protection from fraud and it does not certify safety.

sections.heading: What the drill keeps
sections.body: The drill keeps your messages and the debrief so it can show them back to you. A session is deleted automatically after seven days.

sections.heading: What it never asks for
sections.body: There is no account, no email address and no phone number. The drill never asks for an OTP, a card number, a PIN or an account detail, and it warns you if a message looks like one.

sections.heading: Who can read a session
sections.body: Only someone holding the session link or the report link can read it. A report link stops working when it expires, and you can delete the session at any time.

sections.heading: What a family member sees
sections.body: When you create a report link, that person sees the debrief and the transcript. Nothing else is shared.

sections.heading: What is not collected
sections.body: There are no analytics, no advertising trackers and no third party scripts on this page or in the drill.

sections.heading: If something looks wrong
sections.body: Delete the session from the debrief screen and stop using the page. The drill is optional at every step.

sections.heading: What Dry Run is
sections.body: A free practice drill for digital arrest scam calls. The officer, the agency and the case in every drill are fictional.

sections.heading: What it is not
sections.body: It is not legal, financial or security advice, and it is not a substitute for official guidance from a bank, a police service or a government helpline.

sections.heading: No guarantee
sections.body: Practising a call does not prevent fraud. Use the drill as one small rehearsal, not as a promise of safety.

sections.heading: Your session
sections.body: You can delete your session and its debrief at any time. Sessions are removed automatically after seven days.

sections.heading: Fair use
sections.body: Use the drill for yourself and your family. Do not use it to impersonate an agency or to help anyone defraud.

sections.heading: Changes
sections.body: If these terms change, the date at the top of this page changes with them.

not_found.title: That page is not here
not_found.body: The link may be old, or the address may have a typo. The drill is one tap from the start.
